headline: Danaher, the life sciences firm, plans an AI-run lab that designs and tests antibodies automatically, expected to open in early 2027.
score_reason: Official company announcement of a new research facility; the speed claim is the company's own.
importance_line: It shows a large life sciences company moving the making of research tools into automated AI labs, which could speed up lab work for scientists if the company's claim of up to 8 times faster holds, though the lab does not open until early 2027.
summary: Healthcare Digital reports that Danaher, the life sciences firm, has announced plans for its first AI-powered autonomous lab, based at its Abcam unit in Cambridge, UK, to design antibodies and other molecular tools and then build and test each candidate automatically. Danaher's chief executive, Julie Sawyer Montgomery, says the lab could help researchers move from an idea to tested reagents up to 8 times faster, and it is expected to open in early 2027.
notes: Read in full from Healthcare Digital, which names no source; quotes are from Danaher's announcement. Reuters carries the same news (blocked here). Speed claim is the company's.
